papers.title: Efficacy and safety of electroacupuncture for overweight and obese patients with anxiety: a randomized sham-controlled trial.
papers.abstract: Anxiety is a common manifestation in obese patients, and is closely linked to the progression of obesity. While electroacupuncture (EA) has shown efficacy in treating anxiety or obesity, high-quality clinical evidence supporting its effectiveness in obese patients with anxiety is lacking. This study is to investigate the effectiveness and safety of real EA (R-EA) versus sham EA (S-EA) as an alternative therapy for overweight and obese patients with anxiety. This patient-and assessor-blinded, randomized, sham-controlled trial included 72 Chinese adults with a body mass index (BMI) over 25 kg/m2 and anxiety symptoms. Participants were randomly assigned to the R-EA or S-EA groups in a 1:1 ratio. All participants received a total of 24 treatment sessions (administered three times per week for 8 weeks) and underwent a 4-week follow-up period. The primary outcomes were changes in Self-Rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) score and weight after treatment. The secondary outcomes included the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), BMI, waist circumference, and serum levels of adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), cortisol (CORT), fasting blood-glucose (FBG), triglycerides (TG), and total cholesterol (TC). Compared with the S-EA group, the R-EA group showed a significantly greater reduction in SAS score after treatment, with a mean difference (MD) of 7.66 (95% CI: 2.27 to 13.05, P = 0.006). No statistically significant between-group difference was observed for body weight (MD:3.6 kg, 95% CI: -0.86 to 8.06, P = 0.112). For secondary outcomes, the R-EA group showed significant improvements over the S-EA group in STAI-1 (MD:6.61, 95%CI: 1.06 to 12.16, P = 0.02), STAI-2 (MD: 5.51, 95%CI: 0.16 to 10.86, P = 0.044), PSQI (MD: 1.86, 95%CI: 0.55 to 3.17, P = 0.006), CORT (MD:1365.96,95%CI: 886.71 to 1864.21, P < 0.001) and ACTH (MD: 13.88, 95%CI: 4.03 to 23.74, P = 0.006), while BMI, waist, WHR, FBG, TG, TC did not differ significantly between groups (all P > 0.05) after treatment. The proportion of participants achieving the minimal clinically important difference (≥ 5% weight reduction from baseline) was higher in the R-EA group than in the S-EA group (13/36, 36.1% vs. 5/36, 13.9%; χ² = 4.74, P = 0.029). EA significantly improved anxiety and sleep quality in overweight/obese patients with comorbid anxiety after 8 weeks of treatment, while no significant between-group difference was observed for body weight reduction. Exploratory analyses indicated a potential for clinically meaningful weight loss in the R-EA group, which warrant further investigation. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400083594. Registered April 29, 2024, https://www.chictr.org.cn/showproj.html?proj=220741 .

papers.title: Multimodal data integration for diagnosis and risk prediction of major depressive disorder in the UK Biobank.
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) diagnosis currently relies on subjective assessments, limiting early detection and accurate risk stratification. To address this, we developed machine learning models for both prevalent diagnosis and 15-year incident risk prediction using multimodal data from 30,040 UK Biobank participants. We integrated six modalities-proteomics, metabolomics, lifestyle factors, family history, biochemical measures, and polygenic risk scores (PRS)-employing a geographically stratified design with England-based participants for training and those from Scotland and Wales for independent validation. The integrated multimodal model demonstrated superior robustness, yielding a stable mean time-dependent AUC of 0.679 for incident prediction and an AUC of 0.791 for prevalent diagnosis. Crucially, our analysis revealed that modifiable lifestyle factors, particularly sleep patterns, and proteomic profiles consistently outperformed polygenic risk scores, which showed limited independent discriminative ability. Notably, the diagnostic model exhibited high specificity, effectively distinguishing MDD from schizophrenia (AUC = 0.865), bipolar disorder (AUC = 0.799), and anxiety disorders (AUC = 0.729). Feature attribution revealed distinct molecular signatures for disease stages: inflammatory mediators including CTSL and MMP7 dominated diagnosis, whereas markers of neuroplasticity and metabolism such as LRRN1 and LEP emerged as key predictors of future risk. Furthermore, biological enrichment analyses implicated dysregulated immune regulation (specifically neutrophil degranulation), lipid metabolism, and signal transduction pathways, highlighting a potential mechanistic shift from metabolic vulnerability in the risk phase to systemic inflammation in the symptomatic state. These findings demonstrate that integrating multimodal data significantly improves the characterization of MDD, offering a scalable framework for objective biomarker discovery and personalized risk assessment.

papers.title: Associations between biomarkers, muscle function, dynapenia status, fall risk, depressive symptoms, and sleep quality in patients with lower limb osteoarthritis: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Lower limb osteoarthritis is common in older adults. It is associated with pain, functional decline, and psychological distress, all of which can impair sleep. However, few studies have comprehensively examined the biological, functional, and psychosocial factors associated with sleep quality in this population. The present cross-sectional study explored the associations between sleep quality and sociodemographic characteristics, biomarkers, muscle function, dynapenia, fall risk, and depressive symptoms in older adults with lower limb osteoarthritis scheduled for joint replacement surgery. Statistical analyses included chi-square or Fisher's exact tests for categorical variables (e.g., sex, marital status, and education level), independent-samples t-tests or Mann-Whitney U tests for continuous variables (e.g., biomarkers, gait time, and fall risk scores), and multivariable logistic regression analyses to identify factors independently associated with poor sleep quality. Among the 114 participants, 55.3% had poor sleep quality. Poor sleep quality was more prevalent among women, participants who were widowed or divorced, and those with lower educational attainment. In the bivariate analyses, compared with participants with good sleep quality, those with poor sleep quality had lower hemoglobin (Hb) levels (12.66 ± 1.31 vs. 13.59 ± 1.38 g/dL), lower glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels (5.79 ± 0.89 vs. 6.15 ± 0.66%), higher C-reactive protein (CRP) levels (0.27 ± 0.59 vs. 0.12 ± 0.15 mg/dL), longer 6-meter gait times (9.93 ± 6.03 vs. 7.91 ± 4.29 s), and higher fall risk scores (9.21 ± 4.49 vs. 7.02 ± 3.76). Multivariable logistic regression analysis revealed that lower Hb levels (odds ratio [OR] = 0.64, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.45-0.91), lower HbA1c levels (OR = 0.57, 95% CI = 0.33-0.99), and higher fall risk scores (OR = 1.14, 95% CI = 1.02-1.28) were independently associated with poor sleep quality. Sleep quality in older adults with lower limb osteoarthritis is associated with multiple biological, functional, and sociodemographic domains. Lower Hb levels, lower HbA1c levels, and higher fall risk were independently associated with poorer sleep quality. These findings highlight the need for a multidimensional assessment approach for evaluating sleep quality in this population. Additional prospective and multicenter studies are required to confirm the observed associations before routine clinical implementation.

papers.title: Postoperative hemispheric hyperperfusion and status epilepticus after chronic subdural hematoma evacuation: a case report.
papers.abstract: Cerebral hyperperfusion syndrome (CHS) is rarely reported after chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) evacuation. We describe a 40-year-old man who developed right hemispheric swelling, neurological deterioration, generalized seizures, and ipsilateral hyperperfusion on computed tomography perfusion after burr-hole drainage of a right CSDH. The overall clinical and radiological course was most consistent with probable CHS complicated by refractory status epilepticus, although seizure-related ictal or postictal hyperperfusion could not be fully excluded. He required strict blood pressure control, antiseizure therapy, deep intravenous anesthesia, and continuous electroencephalographic monitoring. Serial perfusion imaging showed gradual resolution of the hyperperfusion. He was discharged without neurological deficits and had returned to work with a modified Rankin Scale score of 0 by postoperative day 45. At 1 year, he remained seizure-free after withdrawal of all antiseizure medications, and an outside-hospital 24-hour ambulatory electroencephalography report showed no epileptiform abnormalities.

papers.title: Association between the dietary index for gut microbiota and circadian syndrome: a cross-sectional study from NHANES 2007-2018.
papers.abstract: Circadian Syndrome (CircS) is an epidemiologic construct that combines metabolic abnormalities with features related to sleep and mood and has been associated with adverse health outcomes. The dietary index for gut microbiota (DI-GM) is a dietary proxy index reflecting adherence to dietary patterns potentially related to gut microbial composition, but its relationship with CircS remains unclear. A total of 18,491 adults from NHANES 2007-2018 were analyzed using survey-weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS) modeling, subgroup analysis, and sensitivity analysis. Associations between individual DI-GM components and CircS were further evaluated. Nine machine-learning algorithms were used to assess classification performance and model interpretability based on area under the curve, calibration, decision-curve analysis, and Shapley additive explanations. Mediation analyses were conducted to evaluate whether body mass index (BMI) and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) may partly account for the observed association. Higher DI-GM scores were inversely associated with CircS. Participants in the highest quartile had lower odds than those in the lowest (OR = 0.693, 95% CI 0.603-0.797; P for trend < 0.001). RCS analysis suggested an overall inverse association, with no strong evidence of nonlinearity (P overall < 0.001; P nonlinearity = 0.130). Subgroup analyses indicated possible variation by poverty-income ratio, ethnicity, and education. Several DI-GM components differed by CircS status. Machine-learning models showed moderate classification performance, and the incremental contribution of DI-GM was limited. Mediation analyses suggested that BMI, and to a lesser extent SII, may partly account for the association between DI-GM and CircS. Among U.S. adults in NHANES 2007-2018, higher DI-GM scores were inversely associated with CircS. Further longitudinal studies are needed to clarify the temporal relationship between dietary patterns represented by DI-GM and CircS.

papers.title: Reducing the diagnostic odyssey in childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophy through phenotype-guided genomic evaluation.
papers.abstract: Childhood-onset non-5q spinal muscular atrophies (SMA) comprise a clinically and genetically heterogeneous group of neuromuscular disorders in which molecular diagnosis may be delayed despite increasing access to next-generation and whole-exome sequencing. Although broad genomic testing has transformed diagnostic practice, its interpretation remains highly dependent on detailed clinical characterization. We emphasize the value of phenotype-guided genomic evaluation in children with suspected non-5q SMA. Age at onset, distribution of weakness, tendon reflexes, respiratory and skeletal involvement, creatine kinase levels, electrophysiological findings, family history, and targeted neuroimaging may reveal recognizable genotype-associated patterns that help prioritize candidate genes and facilitate variant interpretation. A recently reported pediatric case series illustrates characteristic associations including scapuloperoneal weakness with TRPV4 variants, congenital hypotonia and arthrogryposis with ASCC1-related disease, lower-extremity-predominant weakness with BICD2, pontocerebellar hypoplasia with VRK1, and bilateral thalamic abnormalities with HEXB variants. Rather than replacing genomic technologies, comprehensive phenotyping provides the clinical framework required to maximize their diagnostic yield. Following exclusion of SMN1-related disease, integrating clinical examination, electrophysiology, neuroimaging, and broad genomic sequencing may help reduce the diagnostic odyssey in childhood-onset non-5q SMA.
papers.journal: Neurological sciences : official journal of the Italian Neurological Society and of the Italian Society of Clinical Neurophysiology

papers.title: Spectral power and functional connectivity alterations in multiple system atrophy revealed by resting-state EEG.
papers.abstract: Multiple system atrophy (MSA) is an aggressive α-synucleinopathy characterized by motor and autonomic dysfunction. Elucidating neurophysiological patterns can provide crucial insights into the underlying neural mechanisms. Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) and fMRI data were collected from 69 healthy controls and 123 MSA patients, comprising a discovery cohort (n = 97) and an independent validation cohort (n = 26). MSA patients showed reduced delta power in the cerebellar, frontoparietal, visual I, and limbic networks, with widespread increases in theta and high gamma power. Amplitude-based connectivity decreased across the alpha, beta, and gamma bands in subcortical, cerebellar, default mode, motor, and visual I networks, with increased theta-band synchrony involving motor, visual II, and frontoparietal networks. These EEG abnormalities were corroborated by fMRI connectivity, highlighting cross-modal consistency. Canonical correlation analysis revealed associations between EEG features and motor/non-motor symptom severity. Interpretable stacking models accurately classified MSA-C and MSA-P subtypes and predicted UMSARS progression in longitudinal follow-up. These findings identified aberrant neural activity and network dysfunction in MSA, highlighting EEG as a promising biomarker for disease monitoring.

papers.title: Intrinsic Sweetness and Sweetness-Enhancing Property of β-Damascone.
papers.abstract: β-Damascone is a naturally occurring aroma compound with pronounced fruity-floral and "sweet-smelling" notes. Although well characterized olfactorily, its gustatory role and sweetness-enhancing property remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the intrinsic sweetness of β-damascone and its ability to enhance sucrose-induced sweetness using an integrative approach combining sensory evaluation, electroencephalography (EEG), molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations. Sensory evaluation showed that β-damascone alone elicited negligible sweetness, but significantly amplified and prolonged sucrose-induced sweetness. EEG measurements further revealed strengthened cortical responses during co-stimulation with sucrose. Using a cryo-EM-derived full-length TAS1R2-TAS1R3-membrane model, molecular simulations demonstrated that β-damascone binds to a peripheral region of LB1-LB2 cleft in TAS1R2 VFD, stabilizing its closed conformation. β-Damascone also facilitated conformational rearrangements associated with receptor activation, including widening of the intracellular G-protein-binding cavity. Collectively, these findings provide mechanistic evidence that β-damascone acts as a synergistic enhancer of sucrose sweetness, supporting its potential for sugar-reduction applications.

papers.title: Identification of associative factors for recurrent respiratory tract infection using machine learning models in preschoolers.
papers.abstract: Childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection (RRTI) poses a significant global public health burden. This study aimed to identify factors associated with RRTI in preschool children using machine learning (ML) and to develop a web-based tool for estimating individualized RRTI probabilities. Two cross-sectional surveys using stratified cluster sampling were conducted in 2020 and 2025. RRTI was diagnosed according to the national criteria issued by the Chinese Medical Association and China Association of Chinese Medicine. Questionnaire data covering demographic characteristics, fetal/neonatal history, and lifestyle factors were collected. Total 15,075 eligible records from two surveys were included, reporting an RRTI prevalence of 14.55%. Ten ML models were trained on 29 candidate variables. The eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) model outperformed the others, yielding an area under the curve of 0.733. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration as the top three associative variables for childhood RRTI. Forward feature selection was applied to derive a parsimonious nine-variable predictive set, which was subsequently deployed as an online application ( https://cipchina.streamlit.app/ ). In a large, population-based cohort of preschool children, three factors (sleep duration, child's age, and screen duration) associated with RRTI were consistently identified across multiple high-performing ML models. This study identified key lifestyle-related factors associated with recurrent respiratory tract infection in preschool children. Ten machine learning models were applied to analyze 29 variables from 15,075 Chinese preschoolers, with further importance interpreted via the SHapley Additive exPlanations. Sleep duration emerged as the primary lifestyle-related factor associated with childhood recurrent respiratory tract infection, followed by child's age and screen duration.

papers.title: Use of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions: an evidence map of systematic reviews.
papers.abstract: There is high- or moderate-certainty evidence that massage therapy is beneficial for certain painful conditions. Massage therapy has also been evaluated for a range of non-painful health conditions, but the extent and certainty of this evidence are less well characterized. We mapped the systematic reviews, conclusions, and certainty (quality or strength) of evidence for outcomes of massage therapy for non-painful health conditions. Computerized search of PubMed, AMED, CINAHL, Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, and Web of Science from July 2018 to July 2024. This evidence map updates a Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) report that covered massage therapy reviews published through July 2018. Study selection included systematic reviews of massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions that formally rated the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting the conclusions. Systematic reviews of sports massage therapy, osteopathy, dry cupping/dry needling, and internal massage therapy (e.g., for pelvic floor pain), and self-administered massage therapy techniques (e.g., foam rolling) were ineligible. Main outcomes and measures include health condition, number of included studies, intervention, comparison group, conclusions, and certainty of evidence. A total of 13 systematic reviews of massage therapy for 8 non-painful adult health conditions were identified. Of 190 full-text reviews, 20 used a formal method to rate the certainty (quality or strength) of evidence supporting their conclusions; 7 reviews overlapped in health condition, resulting in 13 included reviews. Across these, one conclusion about abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation was rated as high certainty of evidence. There were 4 conclusions from 3 reviews rated as moderate certainty of evidence: 2 conclusions in 1 review about acupressure and auricular acupressure for improving sleep quality in patients with cancer, 1 conclusion about acupressure for sleep latency and fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and 1 conclusion about massage improving depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia; all remaining conclusions were rated as low or very low certainty of evidence. Evidence on adverse events was collected by 7 of 13 (54%) reviews; serious adverse events attributed to massage therapy were not identified in those reviews, but adverse event data were often incomplete or inconsistently described. Only a small number of systematic reviews reported high- or moderate-certainty evidence supporting the potential benefit of massage therapy for specific non-painful adult health conditions. High-certainty evidence was limited to abdominal massage therapy for functional constipation, whereas moderate-certainty evidence indicated that acupressure and auricular acupressure may improve sleep quality in patients with cancer, acupressure may improve sleep latency and decrease fatigue in people with chronic kidney disease, and massage therapy may reduce depressive symptoms in individuals living with dementia. For most other non-painful adult health conditions evaluated, available conclusions are supported only by low- or very low-certainty evidence. Additional high-quality research is needed to strengthen the evidence base for massage therapy for non-painful adult health conditions, particularly for conditions and outcomes that currently lack at least moderate-certainty evidence.

papers.title: From Synapses to Circuits: A Systematic Review of How Developmental Ethanol Exposure Alters Excitation-Inhibition Balance.
papers.abstract: Fetal Alcohol Spectrum Disorder (FASD) is a prevalent cause of neurodevelopmental impairment associated with lifelong cognitive and behavioral deficits. These difficulties may arise partly because developmental ethanol exposure disrupts the balance between excitatory and inhibitory (E/I) signaling. Acute ethanol exposure can suppress excitation through NMDA receptors and enhance inhibition through GABA_A receptors, thereby reducing neural activity. However, its longer-term effects on synaptic communication in the developing brain remain unclear. We systematically reviewed studies published from 2000 through December 2025 that used whole-cell electrophysiology to measure excitatory and inhibitory postsynaptic currents (EPSCs and IPSCs) following developmental alcohol exposure. The review was limited to rat and mouse studies because these species are the principal experimental models of developmental ethanol exposure and allow comparisons across established developmental stages. Whole-cell studies were selected because they provide direct, cell-resolved measurements of spontaneous and miniature postsynaptic currents; field recordings, EEG, and other network-level approaches were outside the predefined scope. Twenty-five studies met the inclusion criteria. Sixteen examined inhibitory currents, 20 examined excitatory currents, and nine assessed E/I balance. Most studies reported increased frequencies of miniature or spontaneous IPSCs following developmental ethanol exposure. In contrast, EPSC frequency varied by brain region and developmental time point, with both increases and decreases reported. No consistent directional shift emerged among studies assessing E/I balance. Developmental ethanol exposure therefore appears to alter inhibitory synaptic transmission more consistently than excitatory transmission, while its overall effects on E/I balance are heterogeneous and circuit-dependent. These findings highlight the need for systematic, region-specific, and developmentally targeted studies to clarify how altered synaptic signaling contributes to cognitive and behavioral dysfunction in FASD.

papers.title: Wearable sensing technologies and machine learning for fatigue assessment in sport horses.
papers.abstract: Fatigue in sport horses is a multifactorial phenomenon that critically affects performance, injury risk, and welfare, yet its real-time, field-based assessment remains an unmet challenge. To synthesise evidence on the use of wearable sensors and machine learning for fatigue-related monitoring in sport horses and to identify priorities for future fatigue assessment. Scoping review. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Publications from 2015 to 2026 were identified through Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect. Evidence from 102 publications was synthesised across five sensing modalities-heart rate (HR)/heart rate variability (HRV), thermometry, inertial measurement units (IMUs), surface electromyography (sEMG), and GPS-alongside machine learning applications for feature extraction, state classification, and risk modelling. Our synthesis reveals a fundamental disconnect: while each technology captures distinct physiological or biomechanical correlates of load, including autonomic response, thermoregulatory strain, gait stability, neuromuscular activation, and external workload, none provides a standalone signature of fatigue. Only a minority of studies used fatigue as a direct modelling label, with most relying on proxy outcomes such as asymmetry or performance decrement. The included literature was heterogeneous in sensor modalities, study designs, outcome measures, and application contexts. In addition, the limited use of directly defined fatigue outcomes restricted comparison across studies and constrained conclusions regarding fatigue-specific monitoring. The path forward lies not in developing yet another single-sensor solution, but in establishing a multidimensional, context-aware framework that integrates complementary data streams, individualised baselines, and interpretable models. Future research should prioritise: (1) operationalised fatigue definitions; (2) longitudinal, within-horse monitoring designs; (3) robust multimodal fusion architectures; (4) rigorous external validation across equestrian disciplines; and (5) explainable artificial intelligence to bridge the gap between algorithmic output and actionable training decisions.

papers.title: [Research progress on genome-wide association study of circadian chronotype in adolescents].
papers.abstract: Circadian chronotype refers to stable individual differences in sleep-wake cycles and activity timing preferences, and is closely associated with sleep patterns, behavioral characteristics, and mental health. In recent years, with the rapid development of genome-wide association studies (GWAS), increasing attention has been paid to the genetic basis of chronotype. Previous studies have demonstrated that chronotype is highly heritable, and GWAS have identified multiple genetic variants associated with chronotype in adult populations, involving core circadian clock genes, neurotransmitter signaling pathways, and protein degradation regulatory pathways. However, adolescence represents a critical period of circadian development and sleep pattern transition, and the genetic regulation and health implications of chronotype in adolescents remain insufficiently understood. Evening chronotype and delayed circadian timing have been closely associated with insufficient sleep, depression, anxiety, attention deficits, and other mental health problems among adolescents. This review summarizes recent advances in GWAS of chronotype, focusing on its genetic architecture, potential regulatory mechanisms, and current evidence in adolescent populations. Furthermore, the associations between chronotype, sleep characteristics, and mental health outcomes are discussed, providing theoretical insights into the genetic mechanisms underlying adolescent circadian changes and their health implications, and supporting the development of individualized prevention and intervention strategies.
papers.journal: Zhonghua yu fang yi xue za zhi [Chinese journal of preventive medicine]

papers.title: The disrupted navigational compass: pathophysiological mechanisms and clinical interventions for spatial navigation deficits.
papers.abstract: Spatial navigation is a higher-order integrative cognitive ability that supports environmental orientation, goal-directed route selection, and adaptive locomotion by integrating spatial memory, multisensory cues, attention, and executive control. Neural systems supporting navigation are also vulnerable to aging and neurodegenerative disease, making navigation a useful domain for linking basic mechanisms with clinically measurable functional impairment. This review summarizes spatial-navigation mechanisms across multiple levels. At the cognitive level, navigation depends on interacting processes including spatial representation, path integration, reference-frame transformation, landmark use, and route planning. At the network level, hippocampal-entorhinal, retrosplenial-parietal, scene-selective, and prefrontal systems contribute complementary functions. At the cellular level, place-, grid-, head-direction-, speed-, and boundary-related representations encode position, heading, self-motion, environmental geometry, and prospective behavior. Clinical and neuroimaging studies indicate that navigation impairment is associated with structural and functional abnormalities, with the strongest diagnostic evidence currently arising from Alzheimer's disease and its prodromal stages. VR-based behavioral assessment and electrophysiological approaches provide complementary means of characterizing navigation phenotypes: VR enables controlled, repeatable, process-sensitive tasks, whereas intracranial and scalp recordings provide neural information at different spatial and physiological scales. No pharmacological agent has been developed or licensed specifically for navigation impairment; current navigation-focused interventions therefore rely mainly on behavioral and VR-based rehabilitation, compensatory strategies, and emerging neuromodulation approaches. Future studies should integrate process-specific behavioral and physiological markers with biomarker-defined clinical cohorts, and use large, randomized, longitudinal studies to establish diagnostic validity, real-world transfer, and mechanism-informed intervention effects.

papers.title: Transcriptomic and behavioral analyses link perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) exposure to circadian and visual pathway disruption in larval zebrafish (Danio rerio).
papers.abstract: Perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA) is a short-chain perfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) detected in fish tissues and environmental matrices, yet its mechanisms of toxicity remain poorly understood. We evaluated developmental, behavioral, and transcriptomic responses in zebrafish (Danio rerio) exposed to 0.1-100µg/L PFBA for seven days. Survival remained above 96%, although a slight reduction (~2%) was observed in exposed groups. Hatching rate and reactive oxygen species levels were unaffected. Behavioral analysis revealed hypoactivity at 0.1 and 1µg/L, restricted to the first dark and first light periods, indicating a non-monotonic concentration-response. RNA-seq identified 3,177, 1,919, and 2,277 differentially expressed transcripts at 0.1, 1, and 10µg/L, respectively. Exposure to 1µg/L altered circadian rhythm and photoperiodism pathways, whereas 10µg/L affected the nervous system, visual perception, and lens development. Circadian-related genes (cry2, cry3b, cryba1a) were differentially expressed, supporting transcriptomic findings and providing mechanistic insight into PFBA-induced behavioral alterations.

papers.title: Nocturnal hypoxaemic parameters from cardiorespiratory holter monitoring are associated with all-cause mortality in post-ischaemic stroke patients: The CHUTE study.
papers.abstract: Stroke affects approximately 140,000 patients annually in France and is the second leading cause of mortality after cancer. Sleep-disordered breathing (SDB), particularly obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA), worsens functional recovery and increases mortality risk after stroke. The objective of this study was to evaluate markers of nocturnal hypoxaemia recorded during cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring in patients hospitalised for a first ischaemic stroke and to assess their association with all-cause mortality. We conducted a retrospective, observational, single-centre longitudinal study including adult patients hospitalised for ischaemic stroke at Saint-Etienne University Hospital (January 2010-December 2020) who underwent cardiorespiratory Holter monitoring. Five nocturnal hypoxaemia markers were analysed: mean nocturnal SpO2, oxygen desaturation index (ODI), time spent with SpO2 below 90% (T90), mean desaturation duration, and mean slope of desaturation. All-cause mortality was ascertained from the French national INSEE death registry (census date: 23 December 2023). Cox proportional hazards models and Kaplan-Meier analyses were performed. Of 3595 patients hospitalised for stroke, 1113 met inclusion criteria (mean age 65.8 ± 14.4 years; 61% male). At census, 288 deaths had been recorded (mean time to death: 1532 days). Mean nocturnal SpO2 below 90% was associated with mortality (HR 1.46; 95% CI 1.04-2.04; p = 0.028). ODI ≥15/h was associated with mortality (HR 1.58; 95% CI 1.24-2.00; p = 0.00016). T90 ≥ 10% was associated with mortality (HR 1.34; 95% CI 1.05-1.72; p = 0.02). Desaturation duration and slope were not significantly associated with mortality. Mean nocturnal SpO2 below 90%, ODI ≥15/h, and T90 ≥ 10% are associated with all-cause mortality in post-ischaemic stroke patients. These markers are readily obtainable by nocturnal oximetry in neurovascular units and may facilitate early identification of high-risk patients.

papers.title: Is sleep bruxism associated with laryngopharyngeal reflux in EPISONO adult general population?
papers.abstract: To evaluate the association between laryngopharyngeal reflux (LPR) and the prevalence of sleep bruxism (SB) in the adult general population. This cross-sectional study was conducted with a sample of 686 adults (380 female and 306 male), with a mean age of 50.1 years, from a total of 712 individuals of the Sao Paulo Epidemiological Sleep Study (EPISONO) performed in 2015, which was a follow-up of EPISONO 2007. Symptoms associated with LPR were assessed using the Reflux Symptom Index (RSI). Sleep bruxism was assessed by self-report, full in-lab polysomnography (PSG) and combined methods. Sociodemographic, behavioral, psychological and clinical variables were used as possible confounders. Adjusted Poisson Regression analysis was used to evaluate the association between LPR and SB. Considering the individuals who presented LPR (17% of the sample), 23.9% presented self-reported SB, 33.6% PSG-based SB and 10.4% assessed by self-report + PSG. In the unadjusted model, individuals with LPR showed a higher prevalence of self-reported SB. However, no significant associations were found for the other SB outcomes. After adjusting for confounders, LPR was not significantly associated with SB occurrence, regardless of the assessment criteria. Among individuals with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), the presence of LPR was associated with a higher occurrence of SB. The presence of LPR was not related to the occurrence of SB. It is possible that the relationship between LPR and SB is not as strong in general population or may only be relevant in specific subgroups of individuals, such as with OSA.

papers.title: Symptom Impact in Angelman Syndrome: Results from the Hope in Action Caregiver Survey.
papers.abstract: Angelman syndrome is a rare neurological disorder with no approved disease-modifying therapies. First-generation treatments are expected to be disease modifying but not curative, highlighting the importance of understanding symptoms with the greatest impact on individuals with Angelman syndrome and their caregivers to support patient-focused drug development. The Hope in Action survey was designed to capture lived experiences and inform an externally led, patient-focused drug development meeting. A global online survey was conducted among primary caregivers of individuals with Angelman syndrome. The survey was developed by a multidisciplinary team with input from advocates, caregivers, and representatives of the US Food and Drug Administration. Caregivers ranked top-3 domains and rated related symptoms affecting individuals with Angelman syndrome and those impacting caregivers; and top-5 priority symptoms to address with a new non-curative therapeutic. Analyses were descriptive. When ranking and rating from lists of high-impact domains and symptoms, 370 caregiver participants most frequently identified communication, daily living skills, gross motor function, and cognition as impactful to individuals living with Angelman syndrome, and patients' independence and communication challenges as impactful to their own caregiver functioning, social participation, and mental health. Priority symptoms to treat with a new therapy included expressive communication, seizures, mobility, sleep, toileting, aggression, balance, and sustained attention/engagement. Through the largest caregiver-reported study on Angelman syndrome symptom impact, we demonstrate an unmet treatment need and a profound impact on individuals and caregivers across a multitude of domains. These findings directly inform patient-focused drug development and reflect alignment of caregiver priorities and outcome measure selection for trials.

papers.title: The Effects of Mind-Body Exercise on the Management of Fibromyalgia Symptoms: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: The FM guidelines recommend that the treatment of FM should be based on nondrug treatment. Currently, more and more forms of MBE are being applied to the management of FM symptoms. However, the efficacy of the different MBE forms is not known. Five electronic databases were searched in the period ending Jan 20, 2026. Randomized controlled trials were selected and screened according to inclusion and exclusion criteria. A total of 20 studies involving 1177 patients with FM were included. MBE significantly improved core symptoms in patients with FM compared to control conditions. For pain reduction, both TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga showed significant benefits (all p < 0.01), with no statistically significant difference between the two subgroups (p = 0.23). Regarding the overall impact of FM, both TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga significantly reduced disease impact (all p < 0.01). The difference between subgroups approached but did not reach statistical significance (p = 0.05). For anxiety symptoms, both MBE subtypes were associated with significant improvements (all p < 0.05), with no significant difference observed between TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga. In terms of depressive symptoms, TC/qigong demonstrated significant improvement (p < 0.01), whereas Pilates/yoga did not yield a significant effect (p = 0.17). However, the difference between subgroups was not statistically significant (p = 0.14). Significant improvements were also observed for sleep quality (p = 0.01), fatigue (p = 0.001), and quality of life (p < 0.01) following MBE interventions. MBE significantly improves pain, fatigue, sleep, anxiety, depression, and quality of life in fibromyalgia patients. Subgroup analyses indicate that TC/qigong and Pilates/yoga show comparable efficacy in pain and anxiety reduction, while TC/qigong may offer additional benefits for depressive symptoms. These findings provide updated evidence with broader outcome coverage and larger average sample sizes compared to previous meta-analyses.

papers.title: Elevated Phosphorylated Tau and Amyloid-Beta 42 in Sleep Apnoea: Evidence From a Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) biomarkers were detected in the cerebrospinal fluid, plasma and brain of obstructive sleep apnoea hypopnoea syndrome (OSAHS) sufferers. The mechanism mediating these changes remains disputed. This study aims to investigate the relationship between chronic intermittent hypoxia caused by OSAHS and AD blood biomarker levels, allowing a better understanding and consideration of the systemic impact of OSAHS on AD development. We searched PubMed, Scopus and Web of Science databases and conducted the research according the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Studies were included if they reported hypoxic parameters in an OASHS group and a control group and analyses of blood biomarker levels including amyloid-beta and tau. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale was used to assess study quality. Eight studies including 435 OSAHS patients and 281 controls were assessed. Pooled analysis showed elevated Aβ42 (SMD = 0.27, 95%(CI) = 0.03 to 0.51, I2 = 56%, p = 0.03), T-tau (SMD = 0.60, 95%(CI) = 0.26 to 0.94, I2 = 63%, p = 0.0006) and p-tau181 (SMD = 0.41, 95%(CI) = 0.03 to 0.80, effect size = 2.12, I2 = 51%, p = 0.03) in the OSAHS group compared with controls, though no difference in Aβ40 (SMD = 0.33, 95%(CI) = -0.27 to 0.94, effect size = 1.09, I2 = 77%, p = 0.28) levels was observed. Reduced mean oxygen saturation is associated with elevated T-tau (SMD = -0.36, 95%(CI) = -0.62 to - 0.10, I2 = 0%, p = 0.007) and p-tau181 (SMD = -0.61, 95%(CI) = -0.96 to - 0.27, I2 = 0%, p = 0.0004) but not with Aβ42 (SMD = -0.19, 95%(CI) = -0.70 to 0.32, I2 = 76%, p = 0.46). Elevated oxygen desaturation index was associated with increased Aβ42 (SMD = -0.37, 95%(CI) = -0.56 to - 0.18, I2 = 49%, p = 0.0001) and T-tau (SMD = -0.54, 95%(CI) = -0.90 to - 0.17, I2 = 58%, p = 0.004). Findings show that chronic intermittent hypoxia is associated with increased blood Aβ42 levels,, but not Aβ40, in the OSAHS group. This may suggest that hypoxia contributes to processes regulating the production and degradation of neurotoxic amyloid-beta peptides. Further experimental investigation is required to determine whether treating OSAHS and restoring optimal oxygen saturation conditions in the brain affects blood Aβ42 levels and whether OSAHS is a modifiable disorder that may increase the risk of developing AD.

papers.title: Anhedonia in Postpartum Depression: The Role of Neuroinflammation and Dopamine Dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Anhedonia is a core symptom of postpartum depression (PPD); however, the underlying neurobiological mechanisms remain poorly understood. Emerging evidence suggests that postpartum biological adaptations, including sleep disruption, stress, hormonal fluctuations, and immune remodeling, may influence neural systems involved in motivation. In this review, we examine neuroinflammation as a potential contributor to maternal anhedonia through its effects on dopamine-dependent reward circuitry. We propose 2 complementary mechanisms by which inflammatory signaling may disrupt motivation: 1) local inflammatory effects within nucleus accumbens microcircuits regulating dopamine release and 2) dysfunction of corticostriatal networks, whereby inflammation impairs prefrontal regulation and reward valuation processes, leading to downstream anhedonia. Furthermore, we review neuroimaging evidence supporting reward system abnormalities in PPD and discuss how multimodal imaging approaches may help distinguish between proposed mechanistic models. Understanding these pathways may facilitate the development of biologically informed interventions targeting maternal anhedonia.

papers.title: Translating Geroscience Into Clinical Practice: Molecular Targets, Emerging Therapies, and Lifestyle Strategies for Healthy Longevity.
papers.abstract: Population aging has intensified interest in interventions that preserve function and delay multiple chronic diseases by modifying the biology of aging. The field now spans molecular geroscience, experimental therapeutics, biomarker development, and preventive medicine, but the maturity of evidence varies substantially. This study aimed to synthesize foundational mechanisms, clinical and translational strategies, and lifestyle determinants relevant to healthy longevity, while distinguishing established practice from emerging or unproven interventions. A critical narrative review of PubMed/MEDLINE and reference lists was conducted from January 2000 through August 2026. Priority was given to consensus frameworks, human randomized trials, prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, and influential mechanistic studies. Evidence was interpreted according to study design, clinical relevance, reproducibility, and safety. The expanded 12-hallmark framework depicts aging as an interconnected network involving genomic damage, impaired maintenance systems, maladaptive stress responses, inflammation, and dysbiosis. Senolytics, epigenetic reprogramming, nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+) augmentation, mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) inhibition, metformin, and spermidine are biologically plausible, but none yet has definitive evidence of extending lifespan in healthy humans. Epigenetic clocks are useful research biomarkers, although a lower clock estimate is not synonymous with rejuvenation or proven risk reduction. By contrast, cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, dietary quality, restorative and regular sleep, avoidance of tobacco, management of cardiometabolic risk, and social connection are supported by much stronger human-outcome evidence. Responsible longevity medicine should integrate geroscience with rigorous preventive care, use biomarkers as adjuncts rather than diagnoses, and reserve experimental geroprotectors for well-designed trials. The near-term opportunity is not radical life extension, but compression of morbidity through scalable, equitable, and evidence-based preservation of health span.

papers.title: Acupuncture-Assisted Zolpidem Tartrate Tapering and Discontinuation in Patients with Chronic Insomnia Disorder Stabilized on Zolpidem: A Study Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of chronic insomnia disorder (CID) is relatively high and increases with age. The use of sedatives, along with the incidence of their adverse effects, is also rising, which can easily lead to health risks and negative outcomes. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of acupuncture-assisted zolpidem tartrate tapering and discontinuation in patients with CID whose insomnia symptoms are clinically stable while taking zolpidem. This study is designed as a single-center, single-blind, randomized controlled trial.Ninety participants will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either the acupuncture group or the sham acupuncture group. Each participant will undergo 24 sessions of either acupuncture or sham acupuncture, in conjunction with zolpidem tartrate tapering therapy, over a duration of 8 weeks, followed by a 4-week follow-up observation period. The primary outcome is the discontinuation rate of zolpidem tartrate at week 8. Secondary outcomes include the reduction rate of zolpidem tartrate, the discontinuation rates at weeks 10 and 12, frequency of zolpidem tartrate use (nights/week), average daily dose (mg/day), total weekly dose (mg/week), Insomnia Severity Index (ISI), Generalized Anxiety Disorder -7 (GAD-7), Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9), Short Form Health Survey-12 (SF-12), sleep diary-related indicators, Dysfunctional Beliefs and Attitudes about Sleep Scale -16 (DBAS-16), Epworth Sleepiness Scale (ESS) and emergency medication usage. Adverse events will also be monitored throughout the study. Efficacy analyses will be conducted on the intention-to-treat population. The findings of the study may provide preliminary evidence for standardized protocols for reducing and ceasing zolpidem tartrate use through acupuncture assistance. Additionally, this research may offer useful references for patients with CID seeking to safely and effectively reduce or discontinue zolpidem tartrate. These findings may inform future clinical research and larger multicenter confirmatory studies. papers.title: Quality of Life as a Pathway Linking Sleep Quality and Depressive Symptoms in Medical University Students: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Depressive symptoms are common among university students and are associated with poor sleep quality. However, it remains unclear whether the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms is direct or operates through quality of life (QOL). Screen time may also be associated with sleep quality. This study examined whether QOL mediates the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms among medical university students, with screen time specified as an upstream behavioral factor of sleep quality. A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 students aged 19-24 years. Sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and QOL were assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale, and WHOQOL-BREF (Taiwan version), respectively. Partial least squares structural equation modeling with 5,000 bootstrap resamples was used to estimate the structural paths and indirect associations. Longer screen time was associated with poorer sleep quality (β = 0.338, p = 0.001). Poorer sleep quality was associated with lower QOL (β = -0.374, p < 0.001), whilst higher QOL was associated with fewer depressive symptoms (β = -0.614, p < 0.001). Although the total association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms was significant (β = 0.327, 95% bootstrap CI [0.120, 0.477], p < 0.001), the direct association was not (β = 0.097, p = 0.212). The specific indirect association through QOL was significant (β = 0.229, 95% bootstrap CI [0.119, 0.327], p < 0.001), consistent with an indirect-only mediation pattern. Sleep quality was indirectly associated with depressive symptoms through QOL within the specified structural model, while longer screen time was associated with poorer sleep quality. These findings highlight QOL as a central consideration in understanding the association between sleep quality and depressive symptoms, alongside screen-use behaviour in relation to sleep health. Longitudinal studies are needed to clarify temporal relationships among these variables.

papers.title: Chemogenetic hyperpolarization in the entorhinal cortex during sleep facilitates delta oscillations and memory consolidation.
papers.abstract: Memory consolidation is a crucial step in long-term memory formation, during which stable memory representations are formed using recently encoded labile memories. The entorhinal cortex (EC) mediates such brain-wide memory reorganization by exhibiting delta oscillations during sleep, through hyperpolarization-activated cyclic nucleotide-gated (HCN) channels. We tested the feasibility of chemogenetically manipulating EC delta oscillations and examined whether such manipulations affect memory consolidation. We demonstrate that membrane hyperpolarization via the activation of the inhibitory chemogenetic receptor hM4Di paradoxically facilitates delta oscillations in the EC by activating HCN channels, whereas membrane depolarization via the activation of the excitatory chemogenetic receptor hM3Dq induces the opposite effect. Furthermore, we show that chemogenetic depolarization during sleep following learning impairs memory consolidation, whereas chemogenetic hyperpolarization enhances it. Our study provides insights into the effects of chemogenetic manipulation on neural oscillations and identifies EC delta as a key regulator of memory consolidation efficiency.

papers.title: Direction-specific effects of biphasic transcranial magnetic stimulation on cortical and cortico-spinal excitability.
papers.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) is a well-established tool for inducing cortical excitation. However, the relevance of current direction on elicited effects is still incompletely understood. Combining TMS with electroencephalography (EEG) and electromyography (EMG) enables non-invasive analysis of evoked potentials both on cortical and peripheral level. In 23 healthy subjects, EEG and EMG responses to biphasic single pulses applied over the left motor cortex with anterior-posterior to posterior-anterior (AP-PA) or PA-AP current direction and 110% resting motor threshold (RMT) intensity were recorded and contrasted between the alternating phases. A cobot-assisted neuronavigation ensured stable coil-placement during the procedure. RMT was lower and EMG latency was shorter for AP-PA currents compared to PA-AP currents, whereas the EMG amplitude did not differ. For EEG responses, local and global evoked activity was higher for mid-components with PA-AP currents. P60 occurred earlier with PA-AP currents and N100 amplitude was higher in amplitude with AP-PA currents. The trial-wise MEP amplitude correlated significantly with P30 in the AP-PA and for both current directions with the N100 amplitude. Our results highlight the directional sensitivity of M1 and the importance of further exploring the role of current direction in TMS protocols to better understand the cortical processes underlying cortico-cortical and cortico-spinal responses.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for identifying overweight or obesity in preschool children: A multi-regional cross-sectional study in Heilongjiang, China.
papers.abstract: To develop and internally validate explainable machine-learning models for identifying current overweight or obesity among preschool children in Heilongjiang, China. This cross-sectional analysis used monitoring data collected in Harbin, Shuangyashan, and Suihua from late August through late November 2020. After excluding 35 children with missing weight measurements, 1228 children were divided into training (860) and internal validation (368) sets before imputation. Overweight or obesity was defined as a body mass index standard deviation score ≥ +1. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression selected predictors for seven models. Five predictors were retained: sleep sufficiency, birth weight, maternal body mass index, weekend moderate-to-vigorous physical activity, and weekend screen time. Random forest had the highest numerical area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (0.82; 95% confidence interval, 0.77, 0.86), lowest Brier score (0.16), highest accuracy (0.76), and highest F1 score (0.62). Weekend physical activity ranked highest in global importance, followed by maternal body mass index. Explainable machine learning may support pre-screening prioritization when anthropometric assessment is unavailable but should not replace measured height and weight or standard body mass index classification. External validation is required.

papers.title: Syndrome-oriented CNS infectious complications after hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation and CAR T-cell therapy, part 1-viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis: recommendations from the Practice Harmonization & Guidelines Committee of the EBMT.
papers.abstract: Viral encephalitis, meningitis, and myelitis are rare but life-threatening complications after autologous or allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation (HSCT) and chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, associated with 30-60% mortality and frequent neurological sequelae. The absence of harmonised definitions and diagnostic criteria contributes to delayed diagnosis, underreporting, and substantial heterogeneity across centres. This EBMT Practice Harmonization and Guidelines Committee expert consensus provides practical recommendations for the definition, diagnosis, treatment, response assessment, and prevention of viral encephalitis/meningitis and viral myelitis, developed through systematic literature review and multidisciplinary expert consensus following EBMT methodology. We propose standardised diagnostic categories for proven and probable viral encephalitis/meningitis and myelitis, alongside a unified diagnostic algorithm integrating clinical assessment, neuroimaging, electroencephalography, cerebrospinal fluid analysis, and targeted virological testing. We highlight key neurotropic viruses for inclusion in initial cerebrospinal fluid multiplex PCR panels, including human herpesvirus 6, herpes simplex virus 1/2, varicella zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, adenovirus, polyomaviruses BK/JC, and selected community-acquired respiratory viruses, such as EV71, and recommend prompt, risk-based empirical antiviral therapy in suspected cases. These recommendations aim to standardise clinical practice, facilitate multicenter research, and improve outcomes. However, many rely on limited observational evidence or expert opinion, underscoring the need for prospective studies.

papers.title: Building and Sustaining a Framework to Expand Pediatric Acupoint Therapies at School-Based Health Centers and an Academic Tertiary Care Children's Hospital in New York City.
papers.abstract: Research has shown that acupoint therapy can be a viable, evidence-based treatment for treating sleep, anxiety, and pain symptoms among children, adolescents, and adults. This article provides a framework to translate acupoint therapy into formalized programs in outpatient and inpatient pediatric settings. The lead author and her team worked together with children and adolescents in urban school-based health centers and a pediatric tertiary care hospital within a large academic urban medical center using different forms of acupoint therapy to support patients in managing a variety of symptoms. We describe the process of developing patient-centered, evidence-based programs with a strong foundation in research, administration, clinical care, and education, and demonstrate how this model can be effective through teamwork, training, and innovation.

papers.title: Choroid Plexus Papilloma Mimicking Chiari II Malformation in an Infant With Myelomeningocele: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: We describe a rare case of an infant with a diagnostic conundrum of apnoeic episodes, on the background of antenatally diagnosed myelomeningocele and Chiari II malformation (CM2). The infant underwent extensive neurosurgical interventions in the first few weeks of life and treatment including foramen magnum decompression of CM2 and placement of a ventriculoperitoneal shunt for hydrocephalus, with an incidental finding of a choroid plexus papilloma (CPP) WHO Grade 1. The apnoeic episodes persisted and required multidisciplinary discussion, considering the relative likelihood of competing aetiologies. Investigations eventually led to the finding that urinary tract infection was exacerbating the apnoeic episodes and may have contributed to the frequency or severity of the apnoeic episodes. From a neurosurgical perspective, we discuss whether CM2, the fourth-ventricular CPP, and associated hydrocephalus may have contributed to brainstem dysfunction and respiratory dysregulation. From a neurosurgical perspective, we discuss the potential contributions of CM2, a fourth-ventricular CPP, hydrocephalus, and brainstem dysfunction to the infant's respiratory events. The temporal association between urinary tract infection and increased apnoeic episodes also raises the possibility of bladder-mediated autonomic dysregulation, although a single definitive aetiology was not established.

papers.title: Scalp Acupuncture Facilitating Blood Pressure Control in Pediatric Hypertensive Encephalopathy: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Hypertensive encephalopathy (HE) in pediatric patients is a life-threatening condition requiring prompt and controlled blood pressure reduction to prevent neurological complications. We report a 7-year-old child with chronic kidney disease on continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis who presented with HE complicated by seizures and persistent hypertension despite intravenous nicardipine and multiple oral antihypertensive agents. Adjunctive manual scalp acupuncture was initiated using GV20 (Baihui), EX-HN1 (Sishencong), and additional ashi points. Following treatment, the patient demonstrated a progressive reduction in blood pressure over seven sessions, accompanied by resolution of seizures, improvement in sleep, and reduction of associated symptoms such as neck pain. This improvement enabled gradual de-escalation of intravenous nicardipine and transition to oral therapy. No recurrent neurological events were observed during hospitalization or follow-up. The observed clinical response suggests that scalp acupuncture may have a potential adjunctive role in pediatric HE. Plausible mechanisms include autonomic modulation, attenuation of sympathetic activity, improvement of cerebral blood flow and vascular reactivity, modulation of nitric oxide-related pathways, and neuroprotective or anti-inflammatory effects. The application of scalp acupuncture for pediatric HE may be a promising therapeutic adjuvant in controlling blood pressure. Nevertheless, causality cannot be established from a single case, particularly given concurrent antihypertensive therapy and dialysis-based volume management. Further studies are needed to evaluate its efficacy and safety in this setting.

papers.title: A wearable perspiration biosensor for continuous biomarker monitoring in inflammatory bowel disease: Feasibility, concordance, and exploratory temporal dynamics.
papers.abstract: Serum C-reactive protein (CRP) and faecal calprotectin, used to monitor inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) between endoscopies, require intermittent blood or stool sampling. We assessed whether a skin-worn perspiration sensor could measure CRP and calprotectin continuously; TNFα and IL-6 were exploratory analytes. At three US centres, perspiration biomarkers were recorded continuously for 3-30 days in 52 IBD patients (27 ulcerative colitis, 24 Crohn's disease, 1 indeterminate colitis) and 19-32 days in 9 controls, with serum CRP and faecal calprotectin sampled at baseline and study end. Agreement was assessed using correlation and Bland-Altman analysis; ROC-derived cutoffs matched serum CRP 5 mg/L and faecal 250 µg/g. Circadian rhythmicity and ultradian (4-12 h) power were compared among biochemically active IBD (serum CRP > 5 mg/L; n = 15), inactive (n = 37), and controls. 47 of 52 IBD participants (90.4%) completed the protocol. Across 99 paired observations, perspiration CRP correlated with serum CRP (r = .52-.58); perspiration and faecal calprotectin correlated in ulcerative colitis (r = .59-.62) but not in Crohn's disease. A perspiration CRP cutoff of 1551 pg/mL (serum 5 mg/L) gave 85.7% sensitivity and 89.4% specificity; a calprotectin cutoff of 385 (µg/g)·min (faecal 250 µg/g) gave 92.3% and 67.9%. Negative predictive values were high (95%-97%), positive modest (57%). Circadian MESOR and amplitude of both markers were higher in active than inactive IBD. Ultradian power differed by group for calprotectin (Kruskal-Wallis p = .0005) and CRP (p = .0037)-highest in active disease, lowest in controls-but the active-inactive difference was non-significant after false-discovery-rate correction. Perspiration CRP agreed moderately with serum CRP, and perspiration calprotectin with faecal calprotectin in ulcerative colitis only. Their high negative predictive values support the study as a non-invasive adjunct to, not a substitute for, standard-of-care testing. All findings are preliminary, and the temporal-dynamics results are hypothesis-generating, needing confirmation in a larger, prospectively designed, endoscopy-anchored cohort.
